target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): enable prompt caching for Claude 5 models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`amazon-bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` produces **zero prompt cache hits**
on every call — full context is re-sent each turn, making it ~10–20× more expensive
than `claude-sonnet-4-6` on the same setup (reported in #99305, with Bedrock
`cacheReadInputTokenCount`/`cacheWriteInputTokenCount` both `0` on every call).

Root cause is in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/bedrock-options.ts`:
`supportsBedrockPromptCaching()` is the gate that decides whether the provider
attaches `cache_control` blocks. It recognizes prompt-cache-eligible Claude models by:

- the `"-4-"` id marker (the whole Claude 4 generation, e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6`),
- `claude-fable-5`, `claude-3-7-sonnet`, and `claude-3-5-haiku`.

Claude 5 flagship ids like `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` carry **no `"-4-"`
marker** and match none of the special cases, so the gate returns `false`, no cache
points are injected, and every turn is a cold cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a matcher for the Claude 5 generation family so the gate returns `true` for
`claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-opus-5` / `claude-haiku-5` (and their inference-profile
prefixes and dated variants), mirroring how `"-4-"` catches the 4 generation:

```ts
if (candidates.some((s) => /claude-(?:sonnet|opus|haiku)-5(?![0-9])/.test(s))) {
  return true;
}
```

The negative lookahead keeps a hypothetical future `claude-sonnet-50` from matching
while allowing `-5`, `-5-<minor>`, and `-5.0`. Scope is limited to this one gate; no
change to any other model's eligibility (verified below — `claude-3-5-haiku` and
`claude-sonnet-4-6` stay `true` via their existing rules, `claude-3-haiku` and
non-Anthropic `nova` stay `false`).

## User Impact

Agents on `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` (and other Claude 5 Bedrock inference
profiles) now get `cache_control` blocks attached, restoring prompt caching: lower
cost and faster TTFT on multi-turn sessions. No behavior change for any other model.

## Evidence

Regression test added in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/index.test.ts` next to the
existing Fable eligibility test, asserting the global/regional/dated `claude-sonnet-5`
ids are cache-eligible and that an older un-covered Claude 3 model stays ineligible.
Fails before the fix, passes after.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `supportsBedrockPromptCaching()` now returns `true` for Claude 5
Bedrock inference profiles (`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, etc.), so the provider
attaches `cache_control`/cache-point blocks instead of skipping them.

**Environment tested:** Node v24.18.0 on Windows; production function invoked directly
via `node --import tsx` against the fix branch.

**Steps run after the patch:** Called the actual patched `supportsBedrockPromptCaching`
from `extensions/amazon-bedrock/bedrock-options.ts`, comparing before/after and checking
neighboring models for regressions.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch, the real gate rejected Claude 5:

```text
false    global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
false    us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
true     global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
true     us.anthropic.claude-fable-5
false    amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
```

After the patch (PASS = matches expected eligibility):

```text
PASS true  global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
PASS true  us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
PASS true  eu.anthropic.claude-opus-5
PASS true  global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-20260630
PASS true  global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
PASS true  us.anthropic.claude-fable-5
PASS true  us.anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0
PASS false amazon.nova-micro-v1:0
PASS false us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0
ALL PASS: true
```

**Observed result after the fix:** Claude 5 Bedrock profiles are prompt-cache eligible;
all previously-eligible and previously-ineligible models keep their prior verdict.

**Not tested:** A live Bedrock Converse call confirming non-zero
`cacheReadInputTokenCount`/`cacheWriteInputTokenCount` against a real AWS account was not
run — verification was against the production eligibility gate that controls cache-point
injection.

Closes #99305
